question: How a campaign ends: the VCConfirm dialog (who wins, which faction it names, the two buttons, what Continue leaves), the end date's gates, and the whole of CBackEndIdler - what it shows, from what, and how Exit leaves.

addresses.name: CConfirmVictoryConditionResign_Construct
addresses.comment:
**The VCConfirm dialog, made once by CInGameIdler::ShowVictoryConfirmDialog.** 0x670C20 to `ret 4` at 0x67131A; the idler arrives in ECX, the 0x6C-byte object as the stack argument (the base 0x63D4B0 builds the CEU3Dialog on the `VCConfirm` window of eu3dialog.gui). vftable 0x11CF0CC, idler at +0x68.

**Which faction it names**: walk the game state's list of factions (+0xCE4; node data +0, next +8; axis, allies, comintern in the save's order) and for each take the number of its chosen conditions (manager +0x18[f]) whose met byte (+0x68) is set, where the faction is found in the manager's factions (+0x8); a faction the manager does not hold counts 0. `if (best <= count) {best = count; winner = faction}` - starting from 0, so **a tie goes to the last in the list, and with nothing met it is the last faction of the list (comintern)**. The check that opened the dialog says nothing about who triggered it: this is worked out again here, for the end-date route as well.

**The title**: winner == the played country's faction (+0xD8) -> `CONFIRM_VC_VICTORY` "Victory!", otherwise `CONFIRM_VC_DEFEAT` "Defeat!" - a factionless player holds the null faction and so always sees Defeat (the country's faction pointer is never 0). **The text**: `CONFIRM_VC_TEXT` "\u00a7Y$FACTION$\u00a7W has achieved their victory conditions.\nDo you want to continue playing or resign the current game?", FACTION = the winner's localised name (slot 6, so Axis, Allies, Comintern). Title goes to `Title`, text to `Description`; both rendered with the settings' colours (CSettings +0x6C..). **There is no separate text for the end date**: it says the same thing even when no faction has achieved anything.

The dialog is then placed centred on the screen by its own measured size, overriding the file's -250,-140 CENTER: slot 42 (SetPosition) with x = screen_w/2 - w/2, y = screen_h/2 - h/2, each a truncating int division. Nothing else is set; AgreeButton (VC_RESIGN "Resign", ENTER) and DeclineButton (VC_CONTINUE "Continue", ESCAPE) come from the file.

See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-endgame.md, section A.1.
addresses.evidence: Decompiled whole and the winner loop read on the listing (0x670D50..0x670DA8): the test is `cmp local_38, count; jg` skipping, i.e. local_38 <= count takes the later faction; the chosen vector is manager +0x18 and the met byte +0x68 as in CVictoryConditionManager. The title's comparison is `pCVar2 == pCVar4->Faction` at the top of the branch, pCVar2 being the winner. FACTION is CFaction slot 6 (GetLocalisedName). What would show it wrong: a `>` in place of `<=` at 0x670D9C, which would make it the first of equals.

addresses.name: CInGameIdler::ShowVictoryConfirmDialog
addresses.comment: Slot 75: **the campaign's end.** Called by VictoryConditions_DailyCheck when a faction reaches VICTORY_CONDITIONS_TO_WIN with no scenario, and by CInGameIdler::Update (0x655CF0) on every frame the clock is past the defines' end_date. Once ever for this idler (+0x12E1, cleared by the constructor at 0x64807A and written nowhere else, so a load shows it again): makes the 0x6C-byte dialog of `VCConfirm` through CConfirmVictoryConditionResign_Construct (0x270C20) and adds it (CEU3Idler::AddDialog). Then, on **every** call, where slot 95 (IsPaused, byte +0x12D8) answers not paused, slot 27 (TogglePause) - which in multiplayer posts a CPauseGame command (the 0x5C-byte command FINDINGS-factionplay.md asked about, made at 0x6D7F10 with the local player and 0) and otherwise sets +0x12D8 = 1. **So the game is paused the moment the dialog comes up; Continue only closes the dialog (CEU3Dialog slot 6) and the game stays paused.** Reached through the daily test this runs once (game_finished stops the test), so after Continue the player unpauses and the game goes on. **Past the end date it runs every frame**, from Update and without a gate: the dialog never returns, but any unpause is taken back the next frame, so the clock cannot be run past the end date; the only way on is Resign, from this dialog or the in-game menu. Neither path is single player only. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-endgame.md, section A.2.
addresses.revises: comment only: the dialog's text and buttons were 'identified only'; slot 95 and 27 are named (IsPaused, TogglePause) and the once-only behaviour of each half is settled, with what Continue leaves.
addresses.evidence: Read the body whole (0x671A10..): +0x12E1 test, the dialog's making, AddDialog, the second test on slot 95 and slot 27. fieldchain over [reg+0x12E1] gives three sites, the constructor's clear at 0x64807A, the test and the set here. TogglePause (slot 27) and Unpause read at 0x262FD0/0x24C480. What would show it wrong: a second writer of +0x12E1 (fieldchain finds none) or a gate in CInGameIdler::Update above 0x655C19 (none: from the head of Update every edge lands at 0x655B91, the test's own start).

addresses.name: CBackEndIdler::Update
addresses.comment: Slot 1, the back end's per-frame body; `ret 4`, the argument unread as in every slot 1. Pumps the two sessions (application +0x12C with global 0x1A857BF = 0, +0x130 with 1) - commands that arrive still run - then collects this frame's mouse clicks from the input (+0xC4: slot 8 left, slot 22 right) and whatever slot 8 queued, gives them to the gui (+0xB0, slot 1), and draws: with the device ready (0xA759D0, the render target clear black and the scene begun) the interface and Present. **No part of the game runs here**: nothing calls the tick, the map or the AI, and the only thing that can change the game state while this screen is up is a command through the session. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-endgame.md, section A.3.
addresses.evidence: Decompiled whole, 0x608AF0..0x608E4E (`ret 4`): two PumpCommands, the input slots, the gui's slot 1 at 0x608BAB, 0xA759D0, 0xA73240, 0xA73630, Present; no call into the tick. What would show it wrong: a call to RunHourlyPass (0x282630) or CInGameIdler::Update reached from here (the whole body is read).

addresses.name: CBackEndIdler::SetInput
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CBackEndIdler::SetInput(CBackEndIdler* this, void* input, void* renderer)
addresses.comment: Slot 2, called by CEU3Application::Run's screen swap with application +0xE4 and +0xE8: stores them at +0xC4 and +0xC8. `ret 8`.
addresses.evidence: `mov [ecx+0xC4], arg1; mov [ecx+0xC8], arg2; ret 8`, and the swap at 0xA913EA..0xA9140A pushes the two application fields. What would show it wrong: a different swap passing other arguments (the only caller is that swap).

addresses.name: CBackEndIdler::Enter
addresses.comment:
**Slot 3, everything the end-of-game screen shows; bare `ret` at 0x60BA68.** Builds `back_end` (backend.gui), wires `Exit` to OnExitButton (the glue at +0x5D4), and fills the screen once from the state as it stands - it is not updated afterwards.

- `player_shield`: the played country's flag (slot 53, by id) then the icon's slot 73 (not read); `player_shield_right` is looked up and skipped where null (the file has it commented out). `country_value`: the country's localised name (CountryNameOfCountry). `allies_won`, `axis_won`, `comintern_won` are hidden; `loser_background` is left alone, so it is what shows through unless a `<winner>_won` picture is shown on top of it.
- **Three factions, hard coded in this order: `allies`, `axis`, `comintern`** (FindFactionByName over the ideology groups). Per faction, by the name's own tag: `<f>_icon` frame = the faction's `icon` (+0x3C); `<f>_label` text = the faction's localised name; `<f>_members` a member row (backend_faction_member_entry, a 32x32 flag - the shield of slot 53) for each country in `Members` (+0x28, the list's order); `<f>_goals` a row (end_vc_entry) for each condition in chosen[f] (manager +0x18) in that order, with `name` = GetText(the condition's name), `date` set only where the condition is met - the date it was last met, 'YEAR Mon D' (Date_FormatYearMonthDay(date +0x64, abbreviated 1, with_hour 0)) - and `background` frame 1 (not met) or 2 (met); `<f>_vc` = `END_VICTORY_CONDITIONS` "$NUM$ of $TOTAL$ Victory Conditions" (NUM met among chosen, TOTAL the number chosen, both as the rows counted them); `<f>_vp` = `END_VICTORY_POINTS` "Victory Points: $NUM$" with NUM = Progress (+0xAC) / 1000, truncated; `<f>_progress` (a progress bar: endgame_progress_small) filled by slot 18 with its faction's points * 100 / the three factions' points added together (the bare points * 100 if that sum is 0).
- **The result**, worked out afresh for each of the three: tier 5 unless (a) met >= to_win (manager +0x3C) and met strictly more than the other two: tier 0 if its points are greater than the other two's added together, otherwise tier 1; (b) else if its points are strictly the most: tier 2 if greater than the other two's added together, else, with met strictly the most too, tier 3. Tier 0 = `WORLD_ORDER` "World Order!" with the ideology group's localised name and a space in front (e.g. 'Fascism World Order!' whoever played); tier 1, 2 and 3 = `STRATEGIC_VICTORY`/`STRATEGIC_DEFEAT`, `OPERATIONAL_*`, `TACTICAL_*`, the first word by whether the faction is the played country's own (compared to `CCountry +0xD8`, so a factionless player always sees Defeat); none = `STALEMATE` "Stalemate". The first filled of the slots for tiers 0 to 3 wins, in that order. The three tiers cannot collide because each asks a strict maximum. A faction index of -1 is read only on the arm where the player's faction pointer is 0, which the game does not reach (the null faction is a real object).
- `result` is that text. The winner's `<tag>_won` picture is shown where a tier was reached; `music/victorymarchverdi.mp3` plays where the winner is the player's faction, `music/diesiraeintro.mp3` otherwise (`Stalemate` included), when the settings' music volume (+0x80) is above 0.

The file's `factions` list box is not touched: no string names it. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-endgame.md, section A.3.
addresses.evidence: Decoded 0x608E80..0x60BA68 on the listing (the decompiler aliases the stack slots at 0x13C and 0xD8): met stored at [esp+eax*4+0xD8], VP at +0x13C (0x60A5EC, 0x60A5FA), the sum at +0x104, the bar at 0x60A6F6..0x60A76C, the tier ladder at 0x60A84F..0x60A9C9 with to_win at +0x3C of the manager, the 6-slot array at +0x124 with index 5 as the dump, and the WORLD_ORDER branch at 0x60AA68..0x60AB50 taking [esp+0x2C], the group name at +8 and the ' ' string at 0x15B4E94 built left of the text. What would show it wrong: a tier-1 or tier-2 write outside the ladder, or a `result` set elsewhere (the listing's only `result` is 0x60B7EF).

addresses.name: CBackEndIdler::QueueInputEvent
addresses.comment: Slot 8: appends a copy of the 0x1C-byte input event to the frame's list (+0xCC first, +0xD0 last, +0xD4 count, nodes of 0x28 bytes). Update gives the list to the gui and frees it. Two `ret 4` exits. What calls the slot is not traced: *inferred* name.
addresses.evidence: Decompiled whole. The event layout is the eight dwords Update builds for its mouse events. What would show it wrong: the slot being called with something that is not such an event.

addresses.name: CBackEndIdler::GetSession
addresses.comment: Slot 18: the application's session (+0xB8 -> +0x12C), the object CBackEndIdler::Update pumps first. Bare `ret`.
addresses.evidence: `mov eax,[ecx+0xB8]; mov eax,[eax+0x12C]; ret`. One holder in the RTTI tables. Slot 19 beside it is its setter, and the same slot 19 is what ProcessSessionEndRequests calls on the in-game screen to install the placeholder session.

addresses.name: CBackEndIdler::SetSession
addresses.comment: Slot 19: deletes the application's session (+0xB8 -> +0x12C) through its slot 0 where there is one and stores the new one.
addresses.evidence: Decompiled whole, one holder. What would show it wrong: a caller passing anything but a session.

addresses.name: Date_FormatYearMonthDay
addresses.signature: Hoi3CString* __stdcall Date_FormatYearMonthDay(int* date, Hoi3CString* out, int abbreviated, char with_hour) @EAX
addresses.comment: The game's date as text: `sprintf("%d %s %d", year, month, day)`, or with `with_hour` `"%d %s %d %d:00"` - the year first, the month through Date_MonthName (`abbreviated` gives Jan..Dec, otherwise January..December). Year, day and hour are worked out from the tick as elsewhere (43800000 is the null date, 24 ticks a day, 365 days a year, cut). Answers `out`; `ret 0x10`. Callers include the back end's end_vc_entry rows, which ask for 'Year Mon D'. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-endgame.md, section A.3.
addresses.evidence: Decompiled whole; the two format strings are read in place, ret 0x10. What would show it wrong: a caller passing non-tick values.

structs.name: CBackEndIdler
structs.comment: The end-of-game screen (`back_end`, backend.gui): 0x600 bytes, made by CEU3Application::MakeBackEndIdler once RequestGameOver has been acted on. It replaces the in-game screen but does not end the game state, which lives on behind it until Exit; nothing runs but the interface and the session's pump. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-endgame.md, section A.3.
structs.evidence: new(0x600) at 0x6544DE; the RTTI export gives CEU3Idler at offset 0; vftable 0x15CA9B4 (rva 0x11CA9B4) written at MakeBackEndIdler. What would show it wrong: a base at another offset (the export says 0).

struct_fields.name: victory_dialog_shown
struct_fields.comment: Set by CInGameIdler::ShowVictoryConfirmDialog after it has made the VCConfirm dialog, so the dialog comes up once for this idler; cleared only by the constructor (0x64807A), so a load shows it again. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-endgame.md, section A.2.
struct_fields.evidence: fieldchain.py --field 0x12E1 finds exactly the constructor's clear, the test at 0x671A2C and the set at 0x671A66.

struct_fields.name: gui
struct_fields.comment: The gui, set by MakeBackEndIdler; slot 1 is its per-frame update and slot 11 (+0x2C) makes a window from a name. Answered by slot 14 (a folded getter).
struct_fields.evidence: MakeBackEndIdler writes arg3 here; Enter calls [+0xB0]+0x2C with 'back_end'.

struct_fields.name: graphics
struct_fields.comment: CEU3Graphics, set by MakeBackEndIdler (FINDINGS-session2.md section 4); screen size +0x6B9BC/+0x6B9C0, device +0x64.
struct_fields.evidence: MakeBackEndIdler writes the sibling here; Enter reads the screen size off it at 0x608EC8.

struct_fields.name: application
struct_fields.comment: The CEU3Application whose run loop owns this screen; +0x12C its session, +0x130 the other pump, +0xE0 the pending screen. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-endgame.md, section A.3.
struct_fields.evidence: MakeBackEndIdler writes its own this here; OnExitButton's swap at +0x88/+0xE0 and Update's pumps use it.

struct_fields.name: window
struct_fields.comment: The `back_end` window Enter builds: every element Enter sets is found through this. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-endgame.md, section A.3.
struct_fields.evidence: Enter stores the result of the gui's window maker at 0x609072 and uses it for every element look-up.

struct_fields.name: input
struct_fields.comment: From CEU3Application::Run's swap (application +0xE4). Update reads mouse clicks from it (slots 8 and 22).
struct_fields.evidence: CBackEndIdler::SetInput stores it; Update calls [+0xC4]+0x20 and +0x58.

struct_fields.name: renderer
struct_fields.comment: From CEU3Application::Run's swap (application +0xE8). Passed to the gui each frame.
struct_fields.evidence: CBackEndIdler::SetInput stores it; Update passes it to the gui's slot 1.

struct_fields.name: events_first
struct_fields.comment: The frame's input event list, first node (0x28 bytes; next at +0x20). Filled by slot 8 and by Update, freed after the gui has them each frame.
struct_fields.evidence: Update and QueueInputEvent build and free it.

struct_fields.name: events_last
struct_fields.comment: Last node of the list at +0xCC.

slots_noted: Slots 14, 16, 17, 21 and 64 hold folded getters (+0xB0, +0xDC, +0xB4, +0xBC, +0xB8); slot 22 answers +0x258 and slots 28/29 +0x25C (unnamed: only MakeBackEndIdler and Enter touch them); slot 15 answers application +0x124, which FINDINGS-guilive.md left open.
